title: More decisive experiments per day: speed, cheaper tests, and better measurement

brief.state:
Status as of Oct 7, 2:48 PM ET (latest status file in the project; the code copies show no PC run beyond q39). B2 is 3,302,481 params, trained from scratch: 24,000 updates, batch 256. Its 6-seed confirm passed PASS-1 (+20.3 pooled-5 over plain_tf, +6.9 over plain_tf_steps).

Speed is the bottleneck, and the orchestrator's "1 hour" figure is only the fastest run. On the shared 5070 Ti, B2 ran 1.6 to 6.7 updates/s; PC runs took 1.0 to 4.2 h (median about 1.55 h). The 18-run confirm used about 21 run-hours, roughly 7 h at three at a time (computed, ideal packing). Rented 5090s took 0.7 to 1.2 h. No B2 training step has been profiled. custom_io has no torch.compile, CUDA graphs, sequence packing, length bucketing, loader workers or warm starts. Batches pad to their longest prompt (mean prompt 81 characters). Eval is cheap (36 to 158 s per run). A B2 run uses about 3 GB allocated and 4.8 GB reserved; some model shapes reserve 12 to 15 GB.

Measurement. Six-seed pooled-5 SDs: B2 0.63, plain_tf 1.19, plain_tf_steps 1.01; paired SDs 0.94 (B2 minus plain_tf) and 1.33 (B2 minus plain_tf_steps). Two-seed screens matched six-seed means within about 1 point for three arms. Two cheap proxies reversed an arm ordering on one seed each (400-step probe; 8k-step run). A CPU probe on saved checkpoints, with no training, gave clear loop gates. Chain-5 is at ceiling (99.4 to 99.7 for B2), so it cannot show gains. The loops:0 leak is above 5% on 3 of 8 B2 seeds. Null checks reuse six seeds, so their failure rates are rough.

Two findings change the picture. The +6.9 margin is against a step-writing baseline with a 64-character target cap, which left 58 of 72 wrong calculator-on chain rows answer-only; the uncapped control (C0, queue 43) has not run. B2 itself trains 528 rows (9 to 11 program steps) answer-only, because its 7-step program cap drops their program target; that breaks rule 7 and T1 keeps it. Test B1 proved wrong (+0.8 against a +15 mark).

open_questions: Does the step-writing margin (+6.9) survive the uncapped control C0 (queue 43), and does C0 with the calculator reach chain-5 near 98.5?
Would removing B2's 7-step program cap (528 train rows, answer-only today) change B2's chain or family scores? T1 keeps the cap; the fix is untested.
Is B2's step time set by GPU kernels, by per-row Python work (collate, gold, tokenize), or by padded width? No profile exists; a one-step profile on the PC is the cheapest test.
Can batches be length-sorted or packed without changing results? Batch composition changes the data order, so any such change needs paired checks (suggested).
Does training at 6 rounds instead of 8 keep accuracy? The test-time probe says K=6 is 0.6 below K=8, but no model has been trained at 6 (saves about a quarter of loop compute, untested).

How large is GPU nondeterminism (bf16, SDPA)? Needs a same-seed replicate pair per arm; none exists.

Should chain-5 be replaced by a harder panel, since B2 sits at 99.4 to 99.7?
Can the loops:0 leak be held at 5 percent or below on all seeds? It is above on 3 of 8 seeds; the word-pointer hits are the known source (screen report).
Would 1,000-row quick evals (about 10 to 20 s each, computed from the 36 to 158 s final eval) replace the 200-row checks for early decisions? Untested.

Can EGK's NaN be stopped by a loss guard or a lower lr? The runner does not retry failed runs.

Freeze 200 batches of the q33 stream (seed 200) and, for the 8a caps shape (12 loops, 36 registers, 91 numbers, 208 words, 280 chars), 200 batches from the 8a pool. distinct.title: Exact host-side rewrite: row pack, persistent constants, pinned copy
distinct.summary: Each step rebuilds 256 prompts in Python, misses the 20k-entry spans cache about 95% of the time, and makes about 21 host-to-device copies. Build all per-row tensors once, keep constants on the device, move each batch with one pinned copy, and prefetch on a worker. Same batches, same math, so equivalence is a hash and a 1e-5 check, not a 6-seed claim. Build only if idea 1 shows host or sync cost.
distinct.change: Default-off flags, no model-math change. (a) Persistent device buffers (persistent=False) for OMEGA, CONSTS, COMM, POW10 and cached aranges (ledger.py 222, 223, 288, 292, 502; reader.py 86, 88). (b) CIO/data.py build_pack(rows, vocab, MAX_ANS): call the existing collate, Ledger.gold, Ledger.tokenize and CharReader.places on all 200k train rows in 4,096-row chunks, store fixed-width arrays (prompt ids uint8 [N,208], places, spans, nv int64, gold fields bit-packed; about 190 MB), key = sha256(train.jsonl + vocab + MAX_ANS + version), temp-write-then-rename, np.load(mmap_mode='r'); train_batches yields pack.take(idx) with the same RandomState permutation; assert no dev id in the pack. (c) One pinned int64 buffer and one uint8 buffer per step (two alternating sets, CUDA event guard) replacing data.py:131-132, tokenize 5, gold 8, places 1. (d) Optional prefetch worker using the same index stream. (e) Exact forward trims: value_code digits as (a[...,None]//POW10)%10 and (digs[...,None]==arange(10)) instead of the 9-op list comprehension and F.one_hot (8 calls per forward, about 150 fewer ops), and hoisting the constant S0 number-slot keys/values out of the loop. Tier gate from idea 7. Param cost 0.
distinct.why: Shown: 16 blocking copies in 5 drain groups plus 5 pageable copies per step; the spans cache clears at 20,000 entries against 200,000 prompts (about 95% miss, suggested); gold() and row_targets work per row; the sandbox prep estimate is about 9-10 ms per batch (7% of a 148 ms step), so this is worth building only if the PC profile shows a larger host share (the 8a B2 gap of 0.141 vs 0.092 s suggests it may). Vectorising value_code is exact for integers; hoisting S0 saves about 8% of forward FLOPs at B2's shape and helps only if GPU-bound. A prefetch thread contends with Python dispatch for the GIL (suggested), so the pack is the part with least risk.

area_summary:
The 82 raw ideas reduce to 26 distinct ones (2 dropped). CIO in the files means the custom_io code folder under the scratchpad; PF means /mnt/project-files. Three themes.

Speed. Nothing about B2's step has been profiled, and fact checks refute two brief claims: the step is not sync-free (16 blocking host-to-device copies in 5 drain groups, plus 5 pageable copies), and time per update does not look like a fixed launch cost (it tracks block applications and width). The '1 hour' figure is only the fastest run (median 1.55 h; best sustained 8.5 updates/s); B2 costs about 3x plain at best rates, not 7.8x. A quiet B2 step of 115-172 ms against about 55-75 ms of block compute suggests 40-60% is something else. So profile first (idea 1), measure aggregate throughput at par 1/2/3 (idea 3), and only then build the exact host-side rewrite (10), CUDA graphs (13) or checkpointing (21). Every speed edit should pass a tiered equivalence gate with a measured same-seed twin floor (7), which does not exist yet.

Measurement. Seed pairing buys little (correlation +0.63 vs plain_tf, -0.29 vs plain_tf_steps), row noise is the same size as training noise for small margins, and several sealed marks cannot pass under no change (T1 mark 4 rejects an identical design 88-94% of the time; the family mark's 100% failure is multiplicity over 30 families; the null draws are only 90 distinct combinations). Ideas 2, 4, 5, 6 and 18 fix this with CPU work on saved checkpoints (B2 s200-205 and T1 s200/201 exist locally). Loosening any mark needs Ben's explicit approval and must be sealed before a confirm.

Proxies. No B2 score-vs-step curve exists; the 4k loss ranks arms but not seeds. Ideas 11 and 12 are the valid way to test early stops and shorter budgets.

Gaps: dev and train jsonl are not in this snapshot (every re-score needs a PC copy); plain 200-205 checkpoints are uncertain; no M1 B2 number exists (idea 16); stale premises (C0, U0, W1 are done; T1 screen is NOT SHOWN on the copy mark). Variance reduction beyond forking is thin.
